title: Climbing Stairs
statement: You climb `n` stairs taking 1 or 2 steps at a time. Return the number of distinct ways to reach the top. Order matters.
hints: To reach step n you last came from n - 1 or n - 2.
That is the Fibonacci recurrence. ways(n) = ways(n - 1) + ways(n - 2).
Two rolling variables compute it in constant space. ways(1) = 1 and ways(2) = 2.

approaches.name: Rolling Fibonacci
approaches.explanation: Keep only the previous two answers.

editorial: Let dp[i] be the number of ways to reach step i. The last step is a single step from i - 1 or a double step from i - 2, and those sets are disjoint. So dp[i] = dp[i - 1] + dp[i - 2], with dp[1] = 1 and dp[2] = 2. Only two scalars are required.
